title: Messages Empty Message
prompt: A React messages list needs empty-state text. Write a helper that returns "No messages items" when count is 0 and an empty string otherwise.

explanation.beginner:
Example: messagesEmptyMessage(0) produces "No messages items". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “hides message when items exist”: input [2] produces "". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “hides message when items exist”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
